svg.text: Activation tensors (blue) · weight tensors (grey) · matmuls and element-wise ops (yellow / green) · shapes shown ignoring batch B
Eight matrix products move all the data. Everything else is element-wise (add, LN, GELU, softmax) or just reshape.
① EMBEDDING — gather, not really a matmul
context: T ≤ 1024 rows of wpe available
③ POSITION-WISE MLP — 2 matrix products, applied to every row independently
end of block — loop back 12 times: x'' becomes next block's x
④ FINAL LN + UNEMBEDDING — one matmul into vocab space
matmul #7 (sometimes counted as matmul #8 with c_attn split as 3)
THE EIGHT MATRIX PRODUCTS (per forward pass, per layer where noted)

g.text: produce Q, K, V in one shot (per block)
mix heads back to residual stream (per block)
unembed into vocab (once, weight-tied with wte)
Total matmuls per forward pass: 6 × 12 layers + 1 = 73 big ones.
Embedding lookup isn't usually counted — it is a gather (select rows of wte), not a true matrix product.

svg.text: WHERE THE FLOPS GO (per token, T = 1024 sequence)

g.text: The T² term in attention grows faster than the linear MLP term — it becomes dominant beyond T ≈ 4096 in GPT-2-scale models.

svg.text: PYTORCH AUTOGRAD — forward records a graph, backward walks it in reverse

g.text: During forward, every op above becomes a node in a DAG. PyTorch records:
• the op kind (MmBackward, AddBackward, SoftmaxBackward, LayerNormBackward, …)
• pointers to its input tensors (so their gradients can be written back)
• enough state to compute the VJP (vector-Jacobian product): for Y = X · W, dX = dY · Wᵀ, dW = Xᵀ · dY
At backward, starting from loss.backward(), each node contributes a matmul of roughly the same
cost as the forward matmul it mirrors — so a full training step is ≈ 3 × forward FLOPs (fwd + 2 bwd matmuls per linear).
What the diagram above IS NOT showing (but the autograd graph would):
• bias additions inside every linear (small, flat cost)
• dropout layers between ops (training only — pass-through at inference)
• LayerNorm internals: y = (x − μ) / √(σ² + ε) · γ + β → three internal ops
• Softmax internals: exp → sum → divide; stable form subtracts the max first
• the backward graph itself, which is built implicitly from the forward graph above
• tensor stride / contiguity changes at every `reshape` (view, not copy)

svg.text: Forward = 7 distinct matmul patterns · 6 of them fire inside every transformer block · attention is the only one with T² scaling
